newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude seeks top of recent range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude seeks top of recent range.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ NYMEX crude remains within a trading channel bounded roughly by $19.10 and $20.25. Prices are expected to head towards the top of this channel.
+ Gasoline faces resistance at 63.20 cents and is expected to test this today.
NYMEX crude oil futures were expected to trade higher on Friday despite a slightly weaker opening call and head towards the top of the current trading range, chart analysts said.
June NYMEX crude closed 30 cents a barrel firmer on Thursday at $20.03, while May gasoline was 1.10 cents a gallon up at 62.84 and May heating oil was just 0.24 cents up at 55.89.

"The market is in a nice little trending channel," said Victor Yu at Refco. "Two days ago the sell-off took us near trendline support and we are now looking to work towards the upper end of the trading channel today."
The target for the day was $20.25, he said, adding that major support would be found at around $19.35 -$19.40.
A Washington-based chartist saw resistance at a similar level.
"In general it does not look all that bad. But looking at the daily chart, you are seeing what looks like a correction rather than the beginning of a larger upwards move," he said.
Citing his own model based on Elliott Wave theory, he said: "Starting from December we could be seeing a five wave down complete. This would suggest that the bottom is now in the market."
"But there is a fair amount of divergence in the charts so that would make me rather cautious."

He added that his oscillator models, based on the five-day and 35-day moving averages, were close to neutral, and he suggested that the market was likely to remain bound within its latest trading range approximately between $20.27 and $19.10.
Extra support would lie at around $19.40, he added.
Yu saw important resistance for May gasoline at around 63.20 cents a gallon.
"If we break through that then there may be more of a run-up, towards 64.00."
MeesPierson Derivatives in London, employing their Market Profile chart technique, said they saw resistance on gasoline at 63.00/63.15.
"On the downside, we would probably have to join weakness below 61.35.
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
